content: Ritonavir increases the plasma levels or effects of fexofenadine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Ritonavir elevates the levels or effects of finasteride by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance of this interaction remains unclear. Ritonavir enhances the levels or effects of fluoxetine by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is not well established. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of fluphenazine by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical importance of this interaction is uncertain. Food intake enhances the absorption of ritonavir in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to increased plasma levels. This effect applies only to the oral formulations of ritonavir and the co-administered agent. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ganaxolone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. However, changes in ganaxolone exposure when co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors are not expected to be clinically significant. Ritonavir elevates the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of isradipine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unknown. Ritonavir does not result in clinically meaningful changes in the systemic exposure of ixazomib when co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, as observed in clinical trials. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain. Ritonavir elevates the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical importance of this interaction is unknown. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unclear. Ritonavir enhances the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is not well established. Mefloquine decreases the levels of ritonavir through an unknown mechanism. The clinical importance of this interaction is uncertain. Ritonavir reduces the levels of meperidine by increasing its metabolism. Additionally, ritonavir induces the metabolism of meperidine to normeperidine, which may increase central nervous system (CNS) toxicity. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of montelukast by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. Ritonavir elevates the levels or effects of nifedipine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unknown. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of oxybutynin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unknown. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical importance of this interaction is uncertain. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of risperidone by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. Ritonavir enhances the levels or effects of selexipag by decreasing its metabolism. Co-administration may increase selexipag exposure, but this interaction is likely of minimal clinical significance. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical relevance of this interaction is unknown. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. Ritonavir and abacavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Close monitoring is recommended. Ritonavir elevates the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of abemaciclib is required when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.
